s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with bleeding after trauma, and found in conjunction with other systemic and familial factors
salient_findings: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Patient is a female in her early 50s
Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions bleed occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
Hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
Patient had recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs attributed to functional venous insufficiency
Patient has been wearing compression stockings for years
Family history of similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs, along with a history of intracranial hemorrhage and detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, strongly supports this diagnosis. KRIT1 mutations are commonly associated with cerebral cavernous malformations.

rejected.label: Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome
rejected.why: While this condition involves vascular malformations, the specific genetic finding of a KRIT1 variant and the combination of cutaneous and cerebral manifestations point more towards cerebral cavernous malformation.

rejected.label: Venous malformation
rejected.why: Although sonography demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations, the presence of a KRIT1 variant and the patient's cerebral symptoms suggest a more specific diagnosis than a general venous malformation.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a port-wine stain, which is not mentioned in the patient's description, and is associated with different genetic and clinical features.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves vascular malformations and limb hypertrophy, but the specific combination of cutaneous lesions, cerebral hemorrhage, and KRIT1 mutation in this patient does not align with the typical presentation of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.
